title: Power Automate: self-healing repairs desktop flow selector failures with AI
summary: The briefing's controls, preview licensing, data-handling warnings and roadmap dates are supported. One minor qualification is needed: the general desktop-flow error-handling article lists fewer supported errors than the dedicated self-healing page.

claims.claim: Power Automate for desktop uses AI to identify the intended element and generate an alternative selector when the existing selector fails.
claims.quote: When an existing selector can no longer locate the intended UI element, Power Automate for desktop uses AI to identify the element and generate an alternative selector.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes self-healing as an agentic feature intended to improve desktop-flow resilience against UI or web automation failures.
claims.quote: Self-healing is an agentic feature that improves the resilience of desktop flows by recovering from UI or web automation failures.

claims.claim: The roadmap preview includes an action-level opt-in for automatic recovery attempts.
claims.quote: The preview phase includes an action-level opt-in option for automatically trying to recover from a selector error

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Open questions
claims.claim: General availability is planned to add a flow-level opt-in that logs a working alternative selector without applying it at runtime.
claims.quote: the GA phase will additionally include a flow-level opt-in option to only log the alternative, working selector in case of an error, without applying the fix during runtime.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.where: front matter: targetDate; What's changing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The general availability target is March CY2027.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "March CY2027"

claims.claim: The roadmap preview date is April CY2026.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "April CY2026"

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant).
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.where: front matter: platforms; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap platform is Desktop.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Desktop"]

claims.claim: The roadmap lists General Availability and Preview release phases.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Self-healing is maker-opt-in per action rather than an automatic change to existing flows.
claims.quote: Enable self-healing per action: ... Open the Error handling settings. ... Turn on Self-healing (Preview).

claims.where: front matter: licensing; Cost and licensing; Scope; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The preview is included for organization premium accounts at no extra cost.
claims.quote: Self-healing in Power Automate for desktop is currently available for organization premium accounts at no extra cost.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Risk assessment; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Preview usage might be subject to service limits or changes.
claims.quote: Usage might be subject to service limits or changes.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Licensing for general availability has not yet been published.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate self-healing general availability licensing meter credits cap log-only tenant disable API. Opened self-healing and power-platform/admin/power-automate-licensing/types; only preview-specific self-healing licensing was found.

claims.claim: Learn documents no self-healing-specific meter, credit rate or cap as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate self-healing general availability licensing meter credits cap; "self-healing" "licensing" "Copilot Credits". Opened self-healing and Power Automate license types; no self-healing meter, rate or cap found.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The Learn feature documentation describes a prerelease preview subject to change.
claims.quote: [This topic is prerelease documentation and is subject to change.] ... This feature is in preview.

claims.claim: For a supported action's Element not found error, handling proceeds through retry policy, self-healing, Set variable / Run subflow rules, and Continue flow run / Throw error.
claims.quote: Retry policy → Self-healing (preview) → 'Set variable / Run subflow' rules → Continue flow run / Throw error

claims.claim: A successful repair uses the alternative selector at runtime and allows the flow to continue.
claims.quote: If the repair succeeds, the flow continues. ... the AI-generated selector that was used at runtime.

claims.claim: Normal error handling resumes if self-healing fails.
claims.quote: If it fails, normal error handling resumes.

claims.claim: Self-healing is runtime-only.
claims.quote: Self-healing is a runtime-only capability.

claims.claim: Self-healing applies to console runs.
claims.quote: It applies to console and cloud (attended and unattended) runs

claims.claim: Self-healing applies to attended cloud runs.
claims.quote: It applies to console and cloud (attended and unattended) runs

claims.claim: Self-healing applies to unattended cloud runs.
claims.quote: It applies to console and cloud (attended and unattended) runs

claims.claim: Self-healing has no effect during designer runs.
claims.quote: has no effect during designer runs.

claims.claim: Self-healing covers only specific UI and browser automation actions interacting with a single UI element.
claims.quote: Is available only for specific UI and browser automation actions that interact with a single UI element (for example, clicking a button or selecting a checkbox).

claims.claim: The dedicated self-healing page lists Element not found and Window not found as supported errors.
claims.quote: Applies only to Element not found and Window not found errors.
claims.fix: After the supported-error sentence, add: 'The general error-handling article still lists only Element not found errors, whereas the dedicated self-healing page lists both.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/desktop-flows/errors#configure-error-handling-functionality, which says 'applies only to Element not found errors'.

claims.claim: Element not found errors are captured on primary and secondary screens.
claims.quote: Element not found errors are captured in both primary and secondary screens

claims.claim: Window not found errors are captured only when the window is found on the main screen.
claims.quote: Window not found errors are only captured when the window is found in the main screen.

claims.claim: Self-healing does not apply to window or screen handling actions.
claims.quote: Doesn't apply to window or screen handling actions

claims.claim: Self-healing does not apply to multiple-element actions such as Drag and drop UI element in window.
claims.quote: Doesn't apply to ... actions that interact with multiple elements like 'Drag and drop UI element in window'.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; Governance guidance; controls[5].note
claims.claim: The preview requires Power Automate for desktop version 2.66 or higher.
claims.quote: You need version 2.66 or higher for Power Automate for desktop.

claims.claim: Self-healing is not currently available in GCC, GCC High or DoD.
claims.quote: Self-healing in Power Automate for desktop isn't currently available for use in government clouds (GCC, GCC High, DoD)

claims.claim: Self-healing is not currently available in sovereign clouds.
claims.quote: isn't currently available for use in government clouds (GCC, GCC High, DoD) or sovereign clouds.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: When invoked, self-healing captures a screenshot of the missing UI element for AI-assisted identification.
claims.quote: Power Automate for desktop captures contextual information, including a screenshot of the missing UI element ... so that it can identify the most likely intended element and recapture its selector.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Self-healing captures the missing element's parent window title.
claims.quote: captures contextual information, including a screenshot of the missing UI element, the title of its parent window, and the full desktop image

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Self-healing captures the full desktop image.
claims.quote: captures contextual information, including a screenshot of the missing UI element, the title of its parent window, and the full desktop image

claims.claim: GPT-4.1 mini is one of the two models currently used together for self-healing.
claims.quote: Two large language models are currently used in combination to power self-healing, GPT‑4.1 mini and Claude Sonnet 4.5.

claims.claim: Claude Sonnet 4.5 is the other model currently used for self-healing.
claims.quote: Two large language models are currently used in combination to power self-healing, GPT‑4.1 mini and Claude Sonnet 4.5.

claims.claim: Self-healing might identify an unintended UI element.
claims.quote: Because self-healing uses generative AI, it might occasionally identify an unintended UI element.

claims.claim: The Power Automate portal does not currently expose self-healing details in action-level run logs.
claims.quote: The Power Automate portal doesn't currently surface self-healing details in the action-level logs of the flow runs where self-healing was invoked.

claims.claim: The desktop flow run page provides a run-specific self-healing summary.
claims.quote: In the desktop flow run page, you can find a summary of the self-healing activity that corresponds to that specific run

claims.claim: The summary includes details from up to three successful repair attempts.
claims.quote: including details from up to three successful self-healing attempts.

claims.where: Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: The repairWithAIInfo action-log property records repair activity and the selector used at runtime.
claims.quote: a new property called `repairWithAIInfo` displays if a repair attempt was made, whether it was successful or failed, and the AI-generated selector that was used at runtime.

claims.claim: Self-healing action details can be retrieved through local logs on the machine that hosted the run.
claims.quote: retrieve action logs, including the self-healing activity, through local log files on the machine that hosted the flow run.

claims.claim: Setting DisableRunFilesCleanup to 1 under HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Power Automate Desktop\Global preserves Actions.log after runs.
claims.quote: `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE` | `SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Power Automate Desktop\Global` | `DisableRunFilesCleanup` | DWORD ... 1: Flow run action details stored in the `Actions.log` file aren't deleted from the local disk after the run is completed.

claims.claim: A Microsoft 365 AI administrator can enable the model provider.
claims.quote: First, a Microsoft 365 AI administrator enables access to a model provider.

claims.claim: A Power Platform system admin allows the provider's models in environments or environment groups.
claims.quote: Then, a Power Platform system admin allows the provider's models in an environment or environment group.

claims.claim: Environments belonging to an environment group must be managed environments.
claims.quote: Environments in an environment group must be managed environments.

claims.claim: Apply changes publishes the environment-group rules.
claims.quote: To publish the rules to the environments in the group, select Apply changes.

claims.claim: Microsoft enables Anthropic models by default for most commercial-cloud customers, excluding EU/EFTA and UK.
claims.quote: Microsoft enables Anthropic models by default for most customers in commercial cloud (excluding EU/EFTA and UK).

claims.claim: Claude models deployed in Power Platform are excluded from EU Data Boundary commitments.
claims.quote: Claude models deployed in Microsoft offerings such as Microsoft Copilot, Researcher, Copilot Studio, Power Platform, and Copilot in Microsoft 365 apps are currently excluded from the EU Data Boundary

claims.claim: Claude models deployed in Power Platform are also excluded from in-country processing commitments where applicable.
claims.quote: are currently excluded from the EU Data Boundary, and when applicable, in-country processing commitments.

claims.claim: The tenant Anthropic subprocessor control is in Microsoft 365 admin center at Copilot > Settings > AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors.
claims.quote: In Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Copilot > Settings, and then select AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors. Enable the Anthropic provider as a subprocessor for your organization.

claims.claim: The environment Anthropic control is in Power Platform admin center at Copilot > Settings > Power Platform > External models.
claims.quote: In Power Platform admin center, go to Copilot > Settings, and then under the Power Platform section, expand External models and enable Anthropic as a subprocessor at environment or environment group level.

claims.claim: The environment-group Anthropic rule is in Power Platform admin center at Manage > Environment groups > environment group > Add rules > Power Platform Anthropic.
claims.quote: select Manage. ... select Environment groups, and then select the environment group. ... Select the Add rules tab. ... Select the checkbox for each rule that you want to add: Power Pages AI features, Power Platform Anthropic

claims.claim: The environment data-movement control is at Manage > Environments > environment > Generative AI features > Edit > Move data across regions in Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: go to Manage > Environments. Select your environment ... In the Generative AI features card, select Edit. ... select the Move data across regions checkbox.

claims.claim: The tenant Copilot setting is at Copilot > Settings > Power Automate > Copilot in Power Automate > On in Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: In Power Platform admin center, go to Copilot > Settings. Under the Power Automate section, select Copilot in Power Automate, then enable the On check box in the displayed pane.

claims.claim: The maker enables self-healing in Power Automate for desktop at action > Error handling > Self-healing (Preview).
claims.quote: Select a supported UI or browser automation action in the flow designer. ... Open the Error handling settings. ... Turn on Self-healing (Preview).

claims.claim: No API is documented for the Microsoft 365 Anthropic subprocessor setting.
claims.quote: Searched: Anthropic subprocessor settings Microsoft Graph beta API; site:learn.microsoft.com/graph "Anthropic" "settings" API. Opened copilot/implement/connect-to-ai-subprocessor; results documented UI, not an equivalent API.

claims.claim: No API covering the environment Anthropic enablement setting is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Anthropic" "Power Platform" "API" settings environment; Anthropic PowerShell pac admin. Opened external-model guidance, Environment Management Settings tutorial and PATCH reference; no Anthropic setting identifier or call found.

claims.claim: No API covering the environment-group Anthropic rule is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Anthropic" "environment group" "API" "Power Platform"; Anthropic subprocessor settings PowerShell pac admin. Opened allow-llm-generative-responses; searched results included group-management commands but no Anthropic rule configuration call.

claims.claim: No equivalent API for Move data across regions is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Platform Move data across regions generative AI API PowerShell Set-TenantSettings; "Move data across regions" "API". Read geographical-availability-copilot excerpts and Environment Management Settings reference; no equivalent call found.

claims.claim: No API for the Copilot in Power Automate switch is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot in Power Automate" "PowerShell" settings; Power Platform Copilot in Power Automate API Set-TenantSettings. Opened Set-TenantSettings reference and self-healing; no documented request property for this switch found.

claims.claim: No API for the action-level self-healing toggle is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate desktop self-healing enable action API Dataverse Web API setting. Opened self-healing; read errors and desktop-flow schema search excerpts. No action-level self-healing configuration API found.

claims.claim: The provider guidance also gives Copilot > Settings > View all > AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors.
claims.quote: Go to the Microsoft 365 admin center and select Copilot > Settings > View all. ... Select AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors.

claims.claim: External-model guidance also allows changing the provider On or Off under Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features.
claims.quote: select Manage. ... select Environments, and then select the environment. ... select Settings. ... select Product > Features. ... turn each applicable model provider setting On or Off.

claims.claim: The Move data across regions checkbox is not displayed or needed for US cloud regions.
claims.quote: The Move data across regions checkbox isn't displayed or needed for US cloud regions.
